request_ticket.body: Hi, I run a one-man carpentry business and I've had my personal Unlimited Plus line with you for 5 years, plus a tablet line. My accountant says I should move the phone onto a business plan so I can claim it properly at year end. I saw the Business Starter plan online at $40, which is cheaper than what I pay now, so that's a bonus. Can I switch my existing line to that and keep my number? All my customers have that number on the side of my van, so losing it is not an option. I'm still paying off my phone on the 36-month device plan (month 14) and I don't want to pay it off in one go, money is tight until the spring jobs come in. I also don't want the tablet moved, it's my daughter's for school and I'd rather keep that personal. And if there's a business hotspot add-on I'd take that too, because I sometimes send quotes from the laptop on site, but only if it doesn't push the price back up. I don't have a company registration number because I'm a sole trader, but I do have a tax ID for the business, BT-4471902. Let me know what paperwork you need. I can come into the Harbor Street store on a Saturday if that's easier. Thanks, Jonah

history.text: Customer reports internet drops 10-20 times a day for a week, worse when it rains. Router rebooted, ran line test: 'Line test: FAIL - high noise on pair, possible fault in external cabling'. Customer confirmed filters on all phone sockets. She also asked about upgrading to fiber; told her FiberLink isn't available on her street yet. Ticket escalated to Tier 2.

Checked history: technician visit WO-88120 on this line was completed recently for the same symptom (replaced internal socket). System flag 'Repeat dispatch within 30 days: YES'. Customer very unhappy, says the first tech 'barely looked' and was 'in and out in ten minutes'. Tried remote port reset on DSLAM and moved the line to a different port profile; errors continue. Recommending dispatch, needs supervisor approval per TD-3.
Approved repeat dispatch. Please send an external-plant technician this time, not in-home. Priority P3. Also apply a $10 goodwill credit for the repeat issue.
Customer called in, says it's been working perfectly since last night and asks us to hold the visit for a couple of days to see if it stays fixed. Work order WO-88944 placed on hold.

Line test this morning: FAIL - high noise on pair. Customer reports two drops overnight during the rain. Customer now asks us to go ahead with the visit as soon as possible and says she works from home on Tuesdays and Thursdays if that helps with access. Goodwill credit confirmed applied.

email_thread.subject: Price rise on my TV + internet bundle
email_thread.body: Hi, I signed up for the Home Duo bundle (internet 300 + TV Essentials) in March 2025 on a '2-year price lock' - I have the order confirmation. My September bill shows the bundle at $119 instead of $99. The notice I got in July said 'prices for Home Duo are changing on September 1'. I assumed that didn't apply to me because of my price lock. Please restore $99.

Hi Gareth, the July notice went to all Home Duo customers. The increase is due to rising programming costs, which are passed through to TV customers. Your price lock covers the bundle price but the terms allow programming cost adjustments. I've attached the terms.

I read the terms you sent. Section 5.2 says the lock covers 'the monthly bundle price', and 5.4 lets you pass through a 'Broadcast TV Surcharge' as a separate line item. But you didn't add a separate surcharge line - you raised the bundle price itself from $99 to $119. That's exactly what 5.2 says you can't do. Also 5.6 says price-locked customers get notice 30 days ahead, and I got mine in July. I'm not disputing the notice timing, just the change itself. For what it's worth, the internet has been great and I'd like to stay, but not at $119.

Gareth, you're right that the increase was applied to the bundle price line rather than as a surcharge. I've asked billing to review. In the meantime I've credited $20 for September. Billing will confirm by next cycle whether future bills are corrected. I should also be transparent that if billing re-issues the change as a Broadcast TV Surcharge, 5.4 would allow that, subject to the 5.6 notice.

price_lock_terms.5.4: The company may introduce or change a separate Broadcast TV Surcharge line item to reflect programming costs; this surcharge is not part of the bundle price.

booster_policy.B1: Customers with good outdoor but weak indoor coverage and a home broadband connection may receive a free Signal Booster (femtocell) if they have been customers for 6+ months, or if they are on Unlimited Plus or above.
booster_policy.B2: Wi-Fi Calling should be offered to all customers with indoor coverage problems.
booster_policy.B3: Where outdoor coverage is poor, boosters are not effective; offer the coverage guarantee cancellation instead.

sla_claim.claim_text: Our circuit was down on September 10 from roughly 9am until mid-afternoon. We lost a client presentation that was being streamed to investors in Singapore, and the client has since gone with another firm. We want the maximum SLA credit and compensation for the lost contract, which we estimate at $12,000. Please also note that we had two short drops on Sept 3 that each lasted a few minutes; we're not claiming for those, but we want it on record. Frankly we are reviewing our options for next year and this will weigh on the decision. We'd appreciate a call from our account manager rather than an email reply. - Priya Anand, Office Manager

noc_record.cause: Carrier-side line card failure at the Harbor exchange
related_tickets: NOC-5720: unrelated DNS latency alert, closed as false positive

sla_terms.S1: SLA credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for service unavailability. Consequential losses (lost profits, lost contracts) are excluded.
sla_terms.S2: Credits require a claim within 30 days of the incident.
sla_terms.S3: Outages caused by the customer or scheduled maintenance are excluded.
sla_terms.S4: Short interruptions under 1 hour are not counted toward availability claims but are logged on request.
sla_terms.S5: Where a Gold customer has a second outage over 4 hours in the same quarter, the customer may terminate without early termination charges.

state.account_manager_note: This client is up for renewal in November; handle with care. The client's own IT contractor did not touch the circuit on Sept 10. No other outages over 1 hour this quarter.
